summary: This bill amends title 36 of the U.S. Code to designate a white flag with a blue border and centered red star as the official Red Star Service Banner, authorizing its display at family homes, veterans organizations, public buildings, and other sites to commemorate service members, veterans, and first responders who died by suicide, without creating benefits or requiring new funding.

scores.thoughts: Section 3 explicitly states that no additional funds are authorized and the Act must be implemented using existing VA appropriations. This prevents any new spending outlay, giving the bill a minor positive alignment with reducing or constraining government spending.
The bill contains no provisions related to taxes, tax rates, credits, or revenue measures of any kind.

While the banner addresses veteran suicide, the legislation itself only creates a symbolic designation and display rules; it does not alter healthcare coverage, funding, delivery systems, or public vs. private policy.
No provisions address firearms, regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
No provisions relate to immigration, visas, borders, or enforcement.
No provisions address reproductive rights or abortion access.
The bill creates a commemorative banner for service members and veterans but does not authorize, increase, or decrease military or defense spending or programs.
No environmental, regulatory, or climate-related provisions appear in the text.
The legislation is purely symbolic and explicitly disclaims creating eligibility for any VA benefit or assistance program, so it has no effect on welfare, food assistance, or safety-net programs.
No provisions concern schools, funding, choice, or federal education policy.
No provisions address controlled substances, decriminalization, or enforcement.
The bill mentions first responders (including law enforcement) only in the context of eligibility for the commemorative banner; it does not alter sentencing, policing, or justice-system policy.
No trade, tariff, or globalization provisions are present.
By prohibiting new appropriations, the bill marginally supports avoiding additional deficit spending, but the effect is negligible and not a primary purpose.
No provisions address LGBTQ+ legal protections or rights.
No foreign-aid or international-assistance provisions exist.
No voting, election-administration, or election-integrity provisions are included.
No technology, data-privacy, or regulatory provisions appear.
No labor, union, or employment-policy provisions are present.
No provisions address religious exemptions, civil-rights enforcement, or anti-discrimination law.
